dependency_coverage.name: NumStability.HDP.Scalar.Preliminaries.absoluteMoment
dependency_coverage.interpretation: This definition assigns to a real-valued function X and real exponent p the ENNReal-valued lower integral of ENNReal.ofReal applied to |X| raised by Real.rpow.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The second conjunct is exactly the unfolding of this definition, so it holds definitionally for every measure and function whenever p is supplied.
dependency_coverage.source_match: The integrand |X|^p and positive-real exponent match the absolute-moment formula, but the definition uses an ENNReal lower integral and is total for arbitrary measures and functions rather than the source's expectation of a random variable on a probability space.

dependency_coverage.name: NumStability.HDP.Scalar.Preliminaries.expectation
dependency_coverage.interpretation: This is the Real-valued Mathlib integral of an arbitrary real-valued function with respect to an arbitrary measure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It determines both the body of rawMoment and the right side of the first conjunct; its type contains no probability, measurability, or integrability premise.
dependency_coverage.source_match: It resembles Lebesgue expectation on the intended integrable random-variable domain, but its total Real-valued interface for all functions and measures commits to behavior outside the source's stated probability/random-variable context and does not represent an unspecified or extended-valued nonintegrable expectation.

dependency_coverage.name: NumStability.HDP.Scalar.Preliminaries.rawMoment
dependency_coverage.interpretation: This definition maps a natural number n to the Real-valued integral of the pointwise natural power X^n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The first conjunct merely unfolds rawMoment at n, independently of the positive real p used by the second conjunct.
dependency_coverage.source_match: The source defines the ordinary moment at the same positive real p used for the absolute moment. Restricting the ordinary exponent to an unrelated n : Nat, including n = 0, does not preserve either its exponent domain or its identity with p.

dependency_coverage.name: And
dependency_coverage.interpretation: And requires both equality propositions to hold.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It combines the raw-moment and absolute-moment unfolding equalities into one proposition.
dependency_coverage.source_match: The printed sentence presents both definitions together, so conjunction is a reasonable logical packaging; it does not repair the mismatched binders or meanings inside the conjuncts.

dependency_coverage.name: ENNReal
dependency_coverage.interpretation: ENNReal is the extended nonnegative reals, WithTop NNReal, and therefore includes +infinity.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the codomain of absoluteMoment and of the second equality, while the ordinary moment is Real-valued.
dependency_coverage.source_match: The source writes the same expectation operator E for both moment formulas and does not state this codomain split. ENNReal is a defensible completion for a nonnegative possibly infinite integral, but it is an additional convention rather than the literal common expectation semantics supplied by the passage.

dependency_coverage.name: ENNReal.ofReal
dependency_coverage.interpretation: This maps a real number to its nonnegative-real part embedded in ENNReal, truncating negative inputs at zero.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It converts the real rpow value of |X| into the codomain required by lintegral.
dependency_coverage.source_match: For the nonnegative base |X| and positive p the power is nonnegative, so the conversion does not change the intended pointwise magnitude; the ensuing ENNReal codomain remains an extra target convention.

dependency_coverage.name: Eq
dependency_coverage.interpretation: Eq states exact equality between two objects of the same type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Each conjunct asserts exact equality of a named moment definition with its unfolded integral expression.
dependency_coverage.source_match: Exact equality is consistent with the source phrase defined as.

dependency_coverage.name: HPow.hPow
dependency_coverage.interpretation: This selects the heterogeneous power operation supplied by the inferred HPow instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: In the first conjunct its instances specialize it to Real base, Nat exponent, and Real result.
dependency_coverage.source_match: Natural power agrees with X^p only at natural orders; it cannot express the literal ordinary moment for an arbitrary positive real p and is applied to n rather than p.

dependency_coverage.name: LT.lt
dependency_coverage.interpretation: This is the less-than relation selected by the Real order instance.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: The SHA-256-verified first-edition PDF, PDF page 1 / printed page 5, says: For p > 0, the p-th moment of X is E X^p, and the p-th absolute moment is E |X|^p; footnote 1 places X on a probability space and makes it real-valued.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The reviewed declaration is the separately named hdp_01_hdef_hmoments_corrected in the prepared direct packet.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The selected passage, edition, and inherited footnote context are exact and directly relevant.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: One positive real p indexes both the ordinary and absolute moments of a real random variable on a probability space.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The target has arbitrary Measure mu and function X, independent n : Nat and p : Real, a Real raw moment, and an ENNReal absolute moment.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The exponent types and identity, probability/random-variable structure, and result codomains are not preserved.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: The phrase For p > 0 scopes the same p over both definitions.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The target universally quantifies n and p independently; 0 < p does not constrain or identify n.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The quantifier structure allows every pairing of a natural raw order and positive-real absolute order, which is not the source's shared-order definition.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: Footnote 1 specifies a random variable X on a probability space, while the defining sentence requires p > 0 and states no integrability or finiteness condition.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The only side condition is 0 < p; there is no IsProbabilityMeasure condition, no Measurable X, no Integrable condition, and no positivity condition on n.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The target omits the inherited probability and random-variable conditions and applies the positivity condition only to the separate absolute exponent.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: The source supplies both E X^p and E |X|^p for every p > 0.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The absolute formula is present at real p, but the ordinary formula is only the unfolding of rawMoment at an independent natural n.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The ordinary positive-real-order conclusion is absent, so the pair of literal definitions is incomplete.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: E means Lebesgue integration and nonlinear functions bind before it; the same E notation is used for both displayed powers.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: rawMoment uses Nat power followed by a total Real-valued integral, while absoluteMoment uses Real.rpow after abs, ENNReal.ofReal, and ENNReal-valued lintegral.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The absolute integrand is recognizable, but the ordinary operator has the wrong exponent domain and the two target integrals impose different codomain/totalization conventions not stated in the source.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: Each quantity is said to be defined as the displayed expectation.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: Both conjuncts use exact Eq and are combined with And.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: Equality and conjunction are suitable relations for packaging the paired definitions; the failures occur in their operands and binders.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: The same source parameter p has two roles: it indexes the ordinary and the absolute p-th moments.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: n indexes rawMoment while a distinct p indexes absoluteMoment.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The single source order is split into two unrelated objects, so parameter identity and roles are not preserved.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: Both exponents are exactly p with p in (0, infinity).
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The ordinary exponent is n : Nat, which may be zero, and the absolute exponent is p : Real with 0 < p.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The ordinary exponent's type, range, and dependence are wrong even though the absolute exponent is correct.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: The literal context is a real random variable on a probability space and an arbitrary positive-real moment order.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The target specializes ordinary orders to Nat but generalizes mu to any measure and X to any function, and it chooses different result codomains for the two integrals.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: These simultaneous specialization and generalization choices are consequential and prevent equivalence; broader applicability elsewhere does not compensate for the missing positive-real ordinary moments.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: The source permits p > 0 without explaining X^p for negative X and noninteger p and states no finiteness convention for either expectation.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The target avoids the negative-base real-exponent issue by changing the ordinary exponent to Nat, includes n = 0, totalizes the ordinary integral into Real, and gives the absolute integral the extended codomain ENNReal.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: Rather than exposing or uniformly resolving the printed boundary ambiguities, the target silently changes the ordinary domain and adopts asymmetric integral conventions.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: The source definitions are intended to assign moment quantities within the probability/random-variable setting at the stated order.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: Both equalities are exact unfoldings of the local definitions and therefore hold for arbitrary mu and X; the p > 0 hypothesis is unused by the equality itself and has no bearing on the raw n-th moment.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The hypotheses are satisfiable, but definitional reflexivity makes the proposition true without enforcing the source context or the intended shared exponent, so its truth does not certify the literal source semantics.

lean_implies_source.reasoning: The Lean proposition cannot yield the source's ordinary moment formula at an arbitrary positive noninteger real p: its ordinary power is indexed only by an unrelated n : Nat. In particular, choosing p = 1/2 leaves the Lean raw conjunct about some independent natural power and supplies no equality for E(X^(1/2)); the source's same-p coupling is absent. The arbitrary-measure/function and integral-convention changes do not cure this missing case.

source_implies_lean.reasoning: The literal source defines moments of a measurable real random variable under a probability measure with one positive p. It does not imply a universally quantified statement for every measure, every possibly nonmeasurable function, every n including zero independently of p, or the target's specific split between a total Real integral for raw moments and an ENNReal lower integral for absolute moments. These are additional and different claims, not consequences of the printed definition.

findings.source_evidence: The source uses one p > 0, reinforced as p in (0, infinity), in both E X^p and E |X|^p.
findings.lean_evidence: The target uses n : Nat for rawMoment and an independent positive p : Real for absoluteMoment.
findings.impact: The target omits ordinary moments at positive noninteger orders and breaks the required identity between the two p-th moment parameters; neither implication direction holds for the complete claims.

findings.source_evidence: Footnote 1 places X : Omega -> R on a probability space (Omega, Sigma, P), with random-variable measurability inherited from that term.
findings.lean_evidence: The target accepts any Measure mu and any function X over a MeasurableSpace, without probability normalization or Measurable X.
findings.impact: The Lean proposition ranges over objects outside the selected source context and does not encode the defining structural assumptions of expectation for a random variable.

findings.source_evidence: The source calls both quantities expectations/Lebesgue integrals, gives no finiteness hypothesis, and does not state distinct codomains or fallback behavior for nonintegrable functions.
findings.lean_evidence: expectation/rawMoment use a total operator of type (Omega -> Real) -> Real with no integrability premise, while absoluteMoment uses lintegral into ENNReal and can represent +infinity.
findings.impact: The target makes asymmetric, substantive choices about undefined or infinite moments that are not the literal common expectation convention in the passage.

findings.source_evidence: For negative real X and noninteger p > 0, the printed X^p lacks a universally defined real value; the passage also omits an expectation-existence convention.
findings.lean_evidence: The target sidesteps the first issue using a natural raw exponent and resolves the second differently for raw and absolute moments.
findings.impact: A corrected formal result should state an explicit exponent/domain and integral convention, but such a correction must be separately named and cannot be judged equivalent to the literal printed pair.

rationale: The corrected target is internally coherent as two definitional unfoldings, and its absolute-moment integrand faithfully uses |X|^p for positive real p. It nevertheless does not formalize the literal printed pair. The source uses the same positive real p for the ordinary and absolute moments, whereas Lean uses an independent natural n for the ordinary moment and p only for the absolute moment. Lean also drops the probability-measure and random-variable conditions and chooses a total Real integral for raw moments but an ENNReal lower integral for absolute moments. Consequently Lean does not imply the positive-real ordinary definition, and the source does not imply the target's broader domain and specific totalization/codomain conventions. The classification is therefore not-faithful-different.
